facts.claim: TOMSA is a 1% tourism levy charged on the room rate at accommodation businesses that take part; it is voluntary for businesses, compulsory for guests where it is collected, is administered by the TBCSA and passed to South African Tourism, and TOMSA says it is not a tax.

articles/where-to-stay-in-cape-town.html: 1% of the room rate, collected only by hotels that take part
It is voluntary for hotels, but its own FAQ says it is compulsory for guests at every place that collects it.
TOMSA says it is not a tax.

facts.claim: Editors' arithmetic (not an official example): on a R3,000 room, 15% VAT is R450 and a 1% levy is R30, giving R3,480; TOMSA does not say whether its 1% is worked out before or after VAT, so before is assumed.

sources.title: South African Revenue Service: value-added tax

articles/where-to-stay-in-cape-town.html: 15% VAT is R450 and a 1% levy is R30, so the bill is R3,480
a R3,000 room comes to about R3,480
